prompt: What does dependency injection mean in this lesson?
hint: You have done it since lesson 10.

choices.text: A library that loads classes at run time by reflection
choices.why: Hilt works at compile time, and injection needs no library at all.

choices.text: A class is given what it needs instead of fetching it
choices.why: Right: instead of fetching it, as `WeekViewModel` receives its handle.

choices.text: Copying a dependency's code into the app
choices.why: That is vendoring, a different subject.

choices.text: Declaring libraries in `libs.versions.toml`
choices.why: That pins build dependencies; injection is about objects at run time.

prompt: Which mistake does Hilt turn from a run-time crash into a build error?

choices.text: A dependency nothing can build
choices.why: Right: `MissingBinding` stopped the build and named the type.

choices.text: A composable recomposes too often
choices.why: Recomposition is outside what Hilt sees.

choices.text: A string is missing from `values-pt`
choices.why: Missing translations fall back to the default; Hilt has nothing to do with them.

choices.text: A network call times out
choices.why: That happens at run time whatever builds the client.

prompt: A hand-written container builds a new `InMemorySessionStore` inside each ViewModel factory. What does the student see?

choices.text: A build error naming the store
choices.why: Code written by hand is not checked like that; it compiles.

choices.text: The same sessions everywhere, because the class is the same
choices.why: Same class, different instances: each holds its own list.

choices.text: Screens that disagree
choices.why: Right: each screen built its own empty store.

choices.text: A crash when the second screen opens
choices.why: Nothing crashes; the sessions are simply in another object.

prompt: Why does the manifest gain `android:name=".PlannerApp"`?
hint: Which class does Android create first?

choices.text: To rename the app on the home screen
choices.why: The label does that; `android:name` names a class.

choices.text: So the graph exists before any activity
choices.why: Right: that is where the singleton component is born.

choices.text: Because KSP reads the manifest to find modules
choices.why: KSP reads annotations in the source, not the manifest.

choices.text: To export the application to other apps
choices.why: Exporting is an activity's attribute, and the application is never exported.

prompt: `InMemorySessionStore` loses its `@Singleton`. What changes?

choices.text: The build fails with `MissingBinding`
choices.why: Hilt can still build it; the `@Inject` constructor is enough.

choices.text: Nothing, singletons are the default in Hilt
choices.why: Unscoped is the default: a new instance per request.

choices.text: Each request gets a fresh, empty store
choices.why: Right: two screens would no longer share the sessions.

choices.text: The store moves into the ViewModel component
choices.why: It moves nowhere; it is simply not shared.

prompt: The activity Hilt may inject is marked `@___`.
Match each annotation to what it tells Hilt.

pairs.right: Use this implementation for that interface
Call this function to make the type
Which component the answers belong to
One instance for the whole app

right_distractors: Run this module only in tests

prompt: Why is `Clock` given by a `@Provides` function rather than an `@Inject` constructor?

choices.text: It is a JDK class, so there is nothing to annotate
choices.why: Right: there is no constructor of yours to put `@Inject` on.

choices.text: Because `@Provides` makes it a singleton
choices.why: It is unscoped here; `@Provides` says how, not how many.

choices.text: Because interfaces need `@Provides`
choices.why: The interface in this lesson used `@Binds`.

choices.text: Because a clock changes every second
choices.why: The object does not change; the time it reads does.

prompt: Why does the lesson put the store and the clock in two modules instead of one?

choices.text: Hilt allows one binding per module
choices.why: A module can hold any number of bindings.

choices.text: A `@Binds` and a `@Provides` cannot share a file
choices.why: They can, in an abstract class with a companion object; the reason is testing.

choices.text: Tests uninstall whole modules
choices.why: Right: section 07 uninstalls both and binds fakes.

choices.text: To make the build faster
choices.why: Splitting modules does not measurably change the build.

prompt: A `@Singleton` class asks for a screen's `SavedStateHandle` in its constructor. What does Hilt do?

choices.text: Gives it the handle of whichever screen opened first
choices.why: Hilt never guesses across components.

choices.text: Refuses it when the app is built
choices.why: Right: a singleton cannot see a binding of the ViewModel component.

choices.text: Creates a new empty handle for it
choices.why: It creates nothing; the binding is not visible there.

choices.text: Crashes when the class is first used
choices.why: The problem is caught before the app exists.

prompt: What replaced lesson 11's `viewModel(factory = WeekViewModel.Factory)` in the screen?

choices.text: `hiltViewModel()`
choices.why: Right: it finds the factory Hilt generated.

choices.text: `viewModel()` with no argument, which now knows Hilt
choices.why: The plain `viewModel()` would need a factory for constructor arguments.

choices.text: `remember { WeekViewModel(store, clock, handle) }`
choices.why: That builds a ViewModel outside any store, lost at rotation.

choices.text: A `@Provides` function in the activity
choices.why: Activities do not hold `@Provides` functions; modules do.

prompt: Why does `onAdd()` no longer take a date?

choices.text: Because Hilt cannot pass arguments to functions
choices.why: Hilt builds objects; function arguments were never its business.

choices.text: Because the date is now stored in the handle
choices.why: Only the draft is in the handle.

choices.text: It asks the injected `Clock`
choices.why: Right: and a test injects a stopped one.

choices.text: Because sessions no longer have dates
choices.why: They do: `LocalDate.now(clock)`.

prompt: `hiltViewModel()` is called inside an activity without `@AndroidEntryPoint`. When does the mistake show?
hint: One of the few the compiler cannot see.

choices.text: At build time, as a `MissingBinding`
choices.why: The graph is complete; what is missing is the activity's entry point.

choices.text: At run time, naming the missing annotation
choices.why: Right: section 04 says so.

choices.text: Never: Hilt falls back to the default factory
choices.why: There is no fallback; the default factory could not build it.

choices.text: Only on Android 13 and later
choices.why: The Android version has nothing to do with it.

prompt: How many generated Java files did the build of section 04 leave under `generated/ksp/debug` and `generated/hilt`?
What is `Hilt_MainActivity`?
hint: Generated, and `MainActivity` ends up extending it.

choices.text: A test double of the activity
choices.why: It is part of the app, not of the tests.

choices.text: A generated base class that injects the activity
choices.why: Right: that is all `@AndroidEntryPoint` needs.

choices.text: The component that holds the singleton store
choices.why: That is `DaggerPlannerApp_HiltComponents_SingletonC`.

choices.text: A copy of `MainActivity` for older Android versions
choices.why: It has nothing to do with Android versions.

prompt: Put the `MissingBinding` experiment of section 05 in order.
Two modules both `@Binds` an implementation to `SessionStore`. What happens?

choices.text: The last module compiled wins
choices.why: There is no order to win by; Hilt refuses.

choices.text: Each screen gets one at random
choices.why: Nothing in Hilt is random.

choices.text: `DuplicateBindings`, at build time
choices.why: Right: the build names both bindings.

choices.text: The app crashes at start-up
choices.why: It never gets that far; the build fails.

prompt: What does `@BindValue` do in `WeekHiltTest`?

choices.text: Makes the field the graph's answer for its type
choices.why: Right: the fake store and the stopped clock.

choices.text: Copies the field's value into the `SavedStateHandle`
choices.why: The handle is untouched; the field joins the graph.

choices.text: Marks the field as read-only
choices.why: `val` does that; `@BindValue` is about the graph.

choices.text: Runs the field's initialiser on the main thread
choices.why: Threads are not its concern.

prompt: Why is `HiltAndroidRule` given `order = 0` and the compose rule `order = 1`?

choices.text: Rules run alphabetically unless numbered
choices.why: JUnit's default order is not alphabetical, and the point is dependency.

choices.text: The activity needs the graph first
choices.why: Right: Hilt builds the graph first.

choices.text: So the compose rule can uninstall modules
choices.why: `@UninstallModules` does that, on the class.

choices.text: So the test runs faster
choices.why: Order is about correctness here.

prompt: In `WeekHiltTest`, the store starts with 50 and 90 minutes and the test adds 25. What total does the screen show, in minutes?
`@Config(application = ___::class)` makes Robolectric start Hilt's test application instead of `PlannerApp`.
Lesson 13 adds a network client that needs a base URL and a timeout. How should it enter the graph?
hint: It is built with a builder, and tests will want to swap it.

choices.text: `@Inject constructor` on the library's class
choices.why: It is not your class; you cannot annotate it.

choices.text: A `@Provides` in its own module
choices.why: Right: a builder call, in a module a test can uninstall.

choices.text: As a global `object`, like lesson 11's `Stores`
choices.why: That is the wiring this lesson removed.

choices.text: Inside the ViewModel's constructor body
choices.why: Then no test could replace it.

prompt: Which of these did the planner need for Hilt to build `WeekViewModel`? Choose all that apply.
hint: The ViewModel's three arguments, and where it is asked for.

choices.text: A binding for `SessionStore`
choices.why: Yes: `StoreModule`.

choices.text: A `@Provides` for `SavedStateHandle`
choices.why: No: Hilt provides the handle itself, per screen.

choices.text: `@AndroidEntryPoint` on `MainActivity`
choices.why: Yes: `hiltViewModel()` needs it.

choices.text: A `ViewModelProvider.Factory` written by hand
choices.why: No: that is what Hilt generated.
